key_insight: In a sepsis vignette study—not cancer drug discovery—three language models exceeded physicians’ diagnostic accuracy after biomarker disclosure.
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest potential for biomarker-informed sepsis decision support, but do not establish safety or effectiveness in clinical practice.
method: Compared five locally deployed language models with 353 clinicians using identical vignettes.
Evaluated six anonymised real cases before and after biomarker disclosure against Sepsis-3 reference diagnoses.
Varied patient sex, age and language, and assessed reproducibility and confidence calibration.
evidence_signal: After biomarker disclosure, accuracy was 91% for Qwen3.8-27B, 86% for its quantised variant and 83% for Gemma-4-31B, versus 61% for physicians.
watch_item: Only six cases were evaluated in silico; language-related bias and difficulty identifying post-surgical sepsis warrant broader prospective validation.
paper_title: Can Language Models Diagnose Sepsis? A Head-to-Head Evaluation Against 353 Physicians
